title: Establishing finite element–fluid interaction model credibility for a stent‑graft proximal seal zone under migration loading: An ASME V&V 40 end‑to‑end example across four mechanisms and two models
device: Thoracic endovascular stent‑graft proximal seal zone

models.name: Model A — Monolithic FSI with compliant wall
models.what_it_computes: Three‑dimensional monolithic fluid–structure interaction of pulsatile aortic flow with a compliant aneurysmal neck and fabric‑covered stent‑graft; computes time‑resolved proximal seal contact pressure, axial hydrodynamic drag, frictional reserve against migration, and cycle‑wise axial impulse.

models.name: Model B — Partitioned reduced‑order FSI
models.what_it_computes: Partitioned FSI coupling: steady–pulsatile CFD surrogate to shell‑based wall compliance and frictional contact; computes cycle‑averaged axial reaction at the seal, net flow drag, and a slip margin metric used to rank migration resistance.

mechanisms.name: Proximal seal friction reserve (PSF)
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Axial migration is resisted primarily by normal force at the graft–neck interface multiplied by friction; PSF quantifies the margin between available friction and hydrodynamic/structural axial loads.

mechanisms.name: Systolic axial flow drag (AFD)
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Unsteady systolic acceleration produces axial fluid forces on the graft body that can exceed frictional capacity in short or angulated necks, precipitating downstream migration.

mechanisms.name: Taper‑induced wedging dynamics (TIW)
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Conicity of the proximal neck promotes cyclic micro‑slip by wedging/unwedging under pulsation; unfavorable taper reduces effective contact pressure and migration resistance.

mechanisms.name: Asymmetric cross‑flow vortex loading (ACV)
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Arch curvature and off‑axis inflow generate lateral vortical structures that impart combined lateral and axial loads, degrading the stability of the proximal seal under eccentric conditions.

clear_factors: Relevance of the quantities of interest

deviation.detail: Each credibility factor is scored on a private 0–4 numeric scale for every model–mechanism pair: 0=not addressed; 1=minimal; 2=partial; 3=adequate; 4=strong.

sections: Question of Interest (migration resistance of the proximal seal zone under four mechanisms)

Context of Use and Rationale: Use validated FSI models to quantify and rank migration resistance of candidate stent‑graft and seal‑zone configurations under PSF, AFD, TIW, and ACV conditions; simulation results will inform design selection and reduce benchtop iteration for these mechanisms without replacing final regulatory performance testing.
Computational Models and What They Compute

Model Risk Level and Rationale: Model influence=High (simulation outputs are the primary evidence for mechanism‑specific design ranking); decision consequence=High (incorrect ranking could propagate a design susceptible to migration in early clinical use); overall model risk=High‑High under ASME V&V 40.
